Original change's description:
> [Composebox] Route remaining searchbox metrics through common helpers
>
> Add recordCount() to cr_components/composebox/common.ts and use the
> existing recordUserAction()/recordBoolean()/recordEnumerationValue()
> helpers in ntp_searchbox.ts and current_tab_chip.ts instead of calling

>
> The helpers fall back to chrome.metricsPrivate when chrome.histograms
> is unavailable, which is the case in extension pages. This is a step
> towards hosting these components outside of WebUI.
>
> The one behavior change is in voice search: it used to bail out when
> chrome.metricsPrivate was missing, which is the case on
> chrome://omnibox-everywhere.top-chrome since that host isn't in the
> metricsPrivate allowlist. VoiceSearch.Action.{OmniboxPageContext} and
> VoiceSearch.Errors.{OmniboxPageContext}, as well as the
> VoiceSearch.Action and VoiceSearch.Errors aggregates, are now recorded
> there too.

[M157] [omnibox][composebox] Move `aim_app.css` into `omnibox_composebox.css`

Original change's description:
> [omnibox][composebox] Move `aim_app.css` into `omnibox_composebox.css`
>
> `aim_app.css` styles `cr-omnibox-composebox` from the outside
> (`#composebox`, `::part()` rules) and paints the AIM popup surface and
> shadow on `omnibox-aim-app`'s `#content` wrapper. Move the rules into
> `omnibox_composebox.css` as `:host` / inner-element rules so the
> composebox looks the same wherever it is hosted. Follow-up to
> crrev.com/c/8538052.
>
> Key changes:
> - `cr-omnibox-composebox` paints the popup surface and shadow on its
>   own `:host` behind a new `webuiShadowEnabled` property, which the
>   host sets (`omnibox-aim-app` passes `omniboxAimWebUIShadowEnabled`).
> - `aim_app.css` is deleted. Where the shared `composebox.css` styles
>   the same state, the selector is repeated so the rule still wins on
>   specificity and order now that it no longer comes from the outer
>   scope.
> - `omnibox-aim-app` loses the `#content` wrapper and the reflected
>   properties that only existed for `aim_app.css`. It still reflects
>   `webui-shadow-enabled_` for `omnibox_popup_document_style.css`.
> - `aim_app_test.ts` covers the host-passed `webuiShadowEnabled`;
>   comments in `omnibox_popup_shared_style.css` are updated to match.
>
> No intended behavior change.
>

[M157][iOS] Fetch passkey credentials in credential bottom sheet mediators

Previously, the credential suggestion bottom sheet only fetched stored
password credentials and matched suggestions by username, and
displayPasswordDetailsForFormSuggestion: required a
CredentialSuggestionBottomSheetMediator instance. As a result, viewing
credential details from the bottom sheet did not work for passkey
suggestions.

This CL moves credential storage and lookup into
CredentialSuggestionBottomSheetMediatorBase, fetches passkey credentials
via IOSWebAuthnCredentialsDelegate in both
CredentialSuggestionBottomSheetMediator and
PasskeySuggestionBottomSheetMediator, and matches passkey suggestions by
their credential ID.

[M157] Avoid flat tree traversal when unlocking a display lock

Original change's description:
> Avoid flat tree traversal when unlocking a display lock
>
> DisplayLockContext::SetRequestedState() called ForceLockIfNeeded() on
> every state change. ForceLockIfNeeded() walks the flat tree to find out
> if a newly requested lock is on the ancestor chain of the node of an
> active forced update scope. This is not needed when unlocking.
>
> DisplayLockContext::DetachLayoutTree() requests an unlock, and it can be
> called during slot assignment recalc, where flat tree traversal is not
> allowed. The traversal could then recalc the slot assignment of another
> shadow root while the assigned nodes of the slots being recalculated
> were not up to date. As a result, parts of the layout tree were not
> detached when they left the flat tree.
>
> Only call ForceLockIfNeeded() when a lock is requested.
>
> Also make ScrollMarkerGroupData::ChooseMarkerRecursively() more robust.
> It runs after layout, and its flat tree walks must not recalc slot
> assignments. It now ignores scroll markers whose scroll targets are not
> connected, runs on a stable list of scroll markers instead of the live
> focus group, and verifies that no slot assignment recalc happens.
>

[M157] [WebUI Omnibox] show the WebUI context menu on right-click

Original change's description:
> [WebUI Omnibox] show the WebUI context menu on right-click
>
> With the full WebUI omnibox, a right-click on the steady-state location
> bar reached OmniboxViewViews, which showed the native views::Textfield
> menu. That textfield has FocusBehavior::NEVER in this mode and is never
> the thing being edited, so its commands acted on a view the user cannot
> see or edit.
>
> Show the WebUI searchbox's own context menu instead:
>
> * OmniboxViewViews::HandOffContextMenuToWebUI() takes over the context
> menu request. It opens and focuses the WebUI omnibox if it isn't open
> (select all, no suggestions), which also covers requests that don't come
> from a mouse press, such as a two-finger tap or the accessibility "show
> context menu" action. If the popup didn't open, e.g. during the brief
> lockout after a popup state change, it falls back to the native menu.
> Otherwise it asks the popup for the WebUI menu via the new
> OmniboxPopupView::RequestWebUIContextMenu().
>
> * OmniboxFullPopupWebUIContent keeps the request pending and dispatches
> it via RenderWidgetHost::ShowContextMenuAtPoint() once the popup widget
> is active and its <input> is focused in Blink, so the resulting
> ContextMenuParams are editable. The anchor is kept in screen coordinates
> and converted when the menu is shown, once the popup is positioned.
>
> * On Mac/Linux the menu is shown on press, so the hand-off consumes the
> release, as MenuRunner::RunMenuAt() does, and resets the press state so
> OnMouseReleased() does not focus again and drop the request.
>
> * Pending requests are dropped when the popup is hidden or its content
> cleared, when the popup widget loses activation, and in
> OmniboxPopupViewFullWebUI::OnFocus(), so a right-click whose menu was
> never shown cannot pop up on a later focus or re-activation.
>
> * On Mac, also wait until the popup has presented a frame since it was
> shown, via a new OnWidgetPresentedChanged() hook off the presenter's
> existing presentation callback. The native menu's nested run loop
> otherwise starts before the newly shown popup window has committed its
> first frame, which then only appears once the menu closes.
>
> * ShowContextMenuComplete() now passes params.source_type to
> MenuRunner::RunMenuAt() instead of hard-coding kMouse, so keyboard- and
> touch-invoked menus anchor and announce correctly.
>

>   derives its layout mode from `hasAllowedInputs`, handles its own

>   now keys on), and exposes `setContextMenuOpen()`.
> - `omnibox-aim-app` is reduced to a wiring shell: it binds
>   `omnibox_popup_aim.mojom`, forwards `close-composebox` /
>   `context-menu-entrypoint-click` to the handler, and drives the
>   composebox through its public API. `closeOnEscape` stays bound by the
>   host since it depends on which popup hosts the composebox. The
>   reflected properties that `aim_app.css` keys on stay until the
>   stylesheet moves.
> - Test hooks move with the logic: `webui_omnibox_interactive_uitest.cc`
>   sets `hasAllowedInputs` / `setBaseSearchboxLayoutModeForTesting()` on
>   `#composebox`; `omnibox_composebox_test.ts` pins the `loadTimeData`
>   values the constructor reads and accounts for the submit cleanup the
>   shell used to do.

[M157] [3P Autofill] Avoid crash when focusing inputs in extension popups

Original change's description:
> [3P Autofill] Avoid crash when focusing inputs in extension popups
>
> ExtensionViewHost unconditionally attached ChromeAutofillClient to the
> extension popup/side-panel WebContents instead of using
> AutofillClientProvider. On Desktop Android, ThinWebView subsequently
> called TabHelpers::AttachTabHelpers, which:
>  1. Attempted to create AndroidAutofillClient when 3P autofill was
>    enabled, which silently no-oped because ChromeAutofillClient already
>    occupied ContentAutofillClient::UserDataKey().
> 2. Skipped creating ChromePasswordManagerClient because
>    uses_platform_autofill() was true.
>
> When focusing an input field in an extension popup with 1P autofill
> suggestions available, ChromeAutofillClient::ShowAutofillSuggestionsImpl
> created ManualFillingControllerImpl, which unconditionally dereferenced
> a null ChromePasswordManagerClient::FromWebContents(web_contents).
>
> This CL:
> - Uses AutofillClientProvider in ExtensionViewHost so that the created
>   ContentAutofillClient matches the profile's autofill mode.
> - Null-checks ChromePasswordManagerClient in
>   ManualFillingControllerImpl's constructor and GetControllerForTabType
>   in RequestAccessorySheet.
> - Guards GetPersonalDataManager() with HasPersonalDataManager() and
>   avoids downcasting AutofillManager to BrowserAutofillManager when
>   UsesPlatformAutofill() is true in
>   PaymentMethodAccessoryControllerImpl.

[M157] Revert "[net/websockets] Continue without client certificate on CertificateRequest"

Original change's description:
> Revert "[net/websockets] Continue without client certificate on CertificateRequest"
>
> This reverts commit f167c8b90fb7d1078ca5cdf754a52743c1fb051e.
>
> Reason for revert: Calling ContinueWithCertificate(nullptr, nullptr)
> directly in WebSocketStream::Delegate::OnCertificateRequested bypasses
> URLLoaderNetworkServiceObserver::OnCertificateRequested (including
> ClientCertStore lookup and AutoSelectCertificateForUrls enterprise
> policy) and caches a sticky nullptr entry for the target or HTTPS proxy
> host_and_port in the profile-wide SSLClientAuthCache, evicting existing
> authenticated HTTP/2 sessions and preventing subsequent requests from
> presenting a client certificate.
>
> Original change's description:
> > [net/websockets] Continue without client certificate on CertificateRequest
> >
> > In net/websockets/websocket_stream.cc, Delegate::OnCertificateRequested
> > previously called request->Cancel() whenever the server requested a
> > client certificate during TLS negotiation.
> >
> > While WebSockets are subresources and should not display a UI prompt
> > to select a client certificate, canceling the request immediately
> > prevents connections to servers where client certificate
> > authentication is optional (e.g., test environments, corporate
> > proxies, and staging GFEs).
> >
> > Per RFC 8446 (TLS 1.3) section 4.4.2 and RFC 5246 (TLS 1.2)
> > section 7.4.6, if a client does not provide a certificate, it should
> > send an empty Certificate message. If client authentication is
> > optional, the server can proceed with the handshake; if required,
> > the server terminates it.
> >
> > This change replaces request->Cancel() with
> > request->ContinueWithCertificate(nullptr, nullptr), matching the
> > behavior of URLLoader and allowing optional mTLS handshakes to
> > succeed.
> >

[M157] [Signin][Android] Reduce ProfileDataCache updates with IdentityManager

Original change's description:
> [Signin][Android] Reduce ProfileDataCache updates with IdentityManager
>
> With MakeIdentityManagerSourceOfAccounts enabled, every refresh token
> update triggered a full rebuild of ProfileDataCache. When the accounts
> are reloaded, IdentityManager sends a refresh token update for every
> account, so reloading n accounts called toDisplayableProfileData() n^2
> times. That regenerated the round avatar again and again, which is
> expensive.
>
> This CL updates the cache one account at a time when accounts are added
> or updated:
> * onExtendedAccountInfoUpdated() and setBadge(accountId, ...) share a
>   new updateCache(AccountInfo) helper, which updates a single entry and
>   keeps the getAccounts() Promise in sync.
> * onRefreshTokenUpdatedForAccount() ignores accounts that are already
>   cached and adds only new ones.
> * onRefreshTokenRemovedForAccount() still rebuilds the whole cache.
>   Removals are sent only for the removed accounts, so this doesn't
>   cause the quadratic cost.
>
> When the flag is enabled, observers are notified with
> onAccountsUpdated() when a single-entry update adds a new account to the
> list. With AccountManagerFacade as the source of accounts, the full
> rebuild triggered by onAccountsChanged() keeps notifying observers, so
> the callbacks with the flag disabled stay the same.
>

[M157] [lensoverlay] Fix flaky QueryFlowRestartsOnSearchboxFocus browser test

Original change's description:
> [lensoverlay] Fix flaky QueryFlowRestartsOnSearchboxFocus browser test
>
> In
> LensOverlayControllerBrowserPDFContextualizationTest.QueryFlowRestartsOnSearchboxFocus:
>
> After expiring cluster info in State::kOverlay and focusing the
> searchbox (which is a no-op in kOverlay), the test calls
> IssueSearchBoxRequestForTesting("red", ...). With
> kLensOverlayNonBlockingPrivacyNotice enabled by default,
> LensOverlayQueryController::SendContextualTextQuery sees that
> cluster_info_ is empty and calls MaybeRestartQueryFlow(), kicking off a
> second query flow (downscaling/encoding the full image on
> encoding_task_runner_ and compressing the PDF bytes on
> compression_task_runner_).
>
> IssueSearchBoxRequestPart2 transitions controller->state_ to
> State::kHidden synchronously. Because the test only waited for
> controller->state() == State::kHidden, RunUntil exited on the next UI
> thread idle callback while the second query flow's background ThreadPool
> tasks were still in flight.
>
> The test then immediately called
> ResetRequestClusterInfoStateForTesting() (setting
> query_controller_state_ to kClusterInfoExpired) and
> OnFocusChangedForTesting(true) (which early-returned in
> TryUpdatePageContextualization() if the second query flow's page content
> upload was still in progress). When the background full-image encoding
> task from the second query flow subsequently posted back to
> CreateFullImageRequestAndTryPerformFullImageRequest, it hit
> DCHECK_EQ(query_controller_state_, kAwaitingFullImageResponse)
> (kClusterInfoExpired vs kAwaitingFullImageResponse).
>
> Fix this by waiting for all asynchronous requests from each query flow
> (full image, page content update, partial page content, and the
> contextual interaction request) to complete before expiring cluster info
> for the next step, and updating the final expected request count after
> the searchbox focus in State::kHidden from 2 to 3.
>
> Tests are fairly flaky:
> https://ci.chromium.org/ui/test/chromium/%3A%2F%2Fchrome%2Ftest%5C%3Abrowser_tests!gtest%3A%3ALensOverlayControllerBrowserPDFContextualizationTest%23QueryFlowRestartsOnSearchboxFocus%2FAll.0

[M157] [omnibox] Destroy popup widget when hidden externally

Original change's description:
> [omnibox] Destroy popup widget when hidden externally
>
> https://screenshot-v2.corp.google.com/5t7sjilmtqfsg
>
> Reproduction:
> 1. Sign into ChromeOS with 2 users.
> 2. In User 1, open the omnibox.
> 3. Switch to User 2 (ctrl+alt+.)
> 4. Switch to User 1 (ctrl+alt+.)
> The omnibox remains stuck open and detached (see screenshot). It cannot
> be easily dismissed, e.g., by clicking outside of it.
>
> This affects WebUI popup, not full WebUI.
>
> Explanation:
> When switching to user 2, ash's `MultiUserWindowManager` hides user 1's
> windows & widgets, including the omnibox popup. In parallel, when the
> browser window deactivates, the omnibox also updates its internal state
> to represent a closed popup. When switching back to user 1,
> `MultiUserWindowManager` restores user 1's hidden windows & widgets.
> This results in forcing the popup widget visible even though the omnibox
> state still thinks it's hidden.
>
> Considerations:
> - We can't easily change how ChromeOS handles window state. E.g. we
>   can't somehow notify `MultiUserWindowManager` that the omnibox popup
>   need not be restored.
> - Other widgets, like permission popups, and the classic Views popup
>   don't face this issue because their widgets are destroyed on hide and
>   `MultiUserWindowManager` can't restore a destroyed window or widget;
>   whereas the WebUI popup widget is hidden & shown rather than destroyed
>   & recreated.
>
> Fix:
> `OmniboxPopupPresenterBase` now tracks whether it considers the popup
> open. If `Hide()` finds the widget already hidden while the popup is
> open, something else hid it (e.g. `MultiUserWindowManager`), so it
> destroys the widget instead of caching it. `MultiUserWindowManager`
> can't restore a destroyed widget, and the next `Show()` creates a new
> one.
> This isn't ChromeOS-specific, but it only triggers when something
> outside the presenter hid the widget.
>

Original change's description:
> [omnibox] Scroll a handed-off selection into view in the WebUI omnibox
>
> When text is highlighted in the unfocused native omnibox, the range is
> handed off to the Full WebUI omnibox input. selectRange() applied it
> with setSelectionRange(), which never scrolls a text field in Blink, so
> the input kept its previous scroll offset and the highlight could be out

> so it now scrolls back to the start too.

> NOTE: This only guarantees that the start of the highlight is in view. A
> selection that runs into the elided text can still end past the right
> edge, because the native omnibox can't scroll to show it.
> https://crrev.com/c/8548590 (b/572793428) makes the native omnibox
> scroll during a drag and hands off where it scrolled to, so the whole
> highlight shows where it was.

[M157] [omnibox] Make Full WebUI omnibox focus follow the Views omnibox

Original change's description:
> [omnibox] Make Full WebUI omnibox focus follow the Views omnibox
>
> The Full WebUI omnibox popup takes activation while the omnibox is
> focused. The Views omnibox popup never does, so the browser window stays
> active while the user types. That difference caused two bugs:
>
> 1. Code that asks whether the browser window is active saw an inactive
>    window while the user was typing. For example, `BookmarkCurrentTab()`
>    only shows the bookmark bubble in an active window, so Ctrl+D / Cmd+D
>    bookmarked the page without showing the bubble.
> 2. Whether a bubble anchored to the browser window blurred the omnibox
>    depended on per-platform activation checks (Linux window tree host,
>    Windows `GA_ROOTOWNER`, ChromeOS activation client, Mac
>    paint-as-active). On Wayland, an active bubble takes the browser
>    window's activation, so it blurred there and nowhere else. That's why
>    WindowSwitchWhileBubbleActiveDismissesPopup failed on the Wayland
>    bots.
>
> This change:
> - Makes `BookmarkCurrentTab()` check `BrowserWindowInterface::IsActive()`
>   instead of `BrowserWindow::IsActive()`. The former follows
>   paint-as-active, and an active child widget such as the popup keeps
>   the browser window painting as active, so it stays true while the user
>   types. `BrowserWindow::IsActive()` is unchanged, so its other callers
>   still see only the browser widget's activation.
> - Replaces the per-platform checks in `OmniboxPopupFullPresenter` with
>   one rule: the omnibox stays focused only while the browser widget or
>   the popup widget is active. Any other window taking activation,
>   including a bubble, blurs it, as with the Views omnibox. On Linux and
>   Windows, the popup only counts while the browser's platform window is
>   also active, since Desktop Aura can leave the popup active after that
>   window deactivates (crbug.com/572976640). This also removes the
>   browser paint-as-active subscription, which only existed for the
>   bubble case.
> - Keeps one exception on Mac: a focus request made while a bubble
>   anchored to the browser window holds activation can still activate the
>   popup, since paint-as-active counts the bubble there. Without it,
>   Cmd+L with the WebUI toolbar while the bookmark bubble was open showed
>   the popup without giving it keyboard focus. That path doesn't move
>   Views focus, which is what activates the browser window first. A
>   request made while the browser window is active still gives way to a
>   bubble that opens before it runs.
> - Removes the ChromeOS-only //ui/aura and //ui/wm deps that only the
>   removed checks used.
>
